skill.name: controlnet-pose
skill.description: Route pose-conditioned image and video generation through the RunComfy CLI. It selects Kling Motion Control for video pose transfer and Wan 2.2 Animate for stylized animation. It uses Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA for still-image pose, depth, or canny control.
skill.summary: Routes pose, motion, depth, and canny control requests to the matching RunComfy model or workflow guidance.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: I reviewed SKILL.md and found no prompt-injection attempt, hidden exfiltration instruction, or malicious intent. All 62 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documented RunComfy links, sample asset URLs, secure token-storage documentation, and benign model-selection wording. The skill is a transparent networked RunComfy workflow, so users should understand that normal operation depends on the RunComfy CLI and external API.

content.value_statement: Pose-controlled generation often requires choosing the right model and input format. This skill routes image and video requests to RunComfy workflows.
actual_capabilities: Routes video pose-transfer requests to Kling Motion Control Pro or Standard.
Routes stylized character animation requests to Wan 2.2 Animate guidance.
Routes still-image pose, depth, or canny requests to Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for reference videos, character images, and control images.
Explains when multi-condition ControlNet stacks need RunComfy ComfyUI workflows.
Summarizes relevant RunComfy exit codes and troubleshooting paths.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated RunComfy CLI.
Does not generate OpenPose, DWPose, depth, or canny control images itself.
Multi-condition ComfyUI workflows are not reachable through the listed CLI endpoints.
Output quality depends on source media framing, model choice, and hosted asset URLs.

use_cases.title: Transfer video motion to a character
use_cases.description: Map a dance, sport, or gesture video onto a target character image.

use_cases.title: Generate a pose-locked still image
use_cases.description: Use an OpenPose, DWPose, depth, or canny control image for composition control.

use_cases.title: Choose the right RunComfy route
use_cases.description: Compare model options for draft cost, final fidelity, subject style, and input type.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a still-image route
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user with one pose reference image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this pose reference to make a still image. Tell me which RunComfy route to use and what inputs are required.

prompt_templates.title: Plan video pose transfer
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a motion reference video and a character image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Transfer the motion from my reference video to this character image. Recommend the right Kling tier for a draft.

prompt_templates.title: Compare model choices
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs guidance before spending RunComfy credits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Kling Motion Control, Wan Animate, and Z-Image ControlNet for my project. Explain tradeoffs for fidelity, style, and input type.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-condition workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user needs pose, depth, and reference-image control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-condition pose workflow using pose, depth, and a reference image. Identify what must move from CLI to ComfyUI.

output_examples.input: A user has a dance reference video and a mascot image.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Kling Motion Control Pro, with Standard as a lower-cost draft option.

output_examples.input: A user has an OpenPose skeleton and wants a still character image.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA and asks for a hosted control image URL.

output_examples.input: A user wants pose plus depth plus reference-image control.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that multi-condition stacks need RunComfy ComfyUI workflows, not the listed CLI endpoints.

best_practices: Use clean, single-subject reference media with stable framing.
Use only user-approved asset URLs because RunComfy receives the referenced media.
Match the control image type to the selected model route.
anti_patterns: Using Kling Motion Control for still-image pose conditioning.
Sending private or unapproved media URLs to a remote model service.
Expecting CLI endpoints to run complex multi-condition ComfyUI workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls image or video generation with pose, motion, depth, or canny references.

faq.question: Does it create pose skeletons?
faq.answer: No. Create OpenPose, DWPose, depth, or canny control images before using this skill.

faq.question: Which route is best for video?
faq.answer: Use Kling Motion Control for photoreal pose transfer and Wan Animate for stylized character animation.

faq.question: Which route is best for still images?
faq.answer: Use Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA with a compatible control image.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI must be installed and authenticated before model runs.

faq.question: Can it run multi-condition ControlNet stacks?
faq.answer: It can guide them, but those workflows require RunComfy ComfyUI rather than the listed CLI endpoints.
